explanation: Ecologists trace species extinction to five primary threats (percentages represent species affected and exceed 100% due to overlapping threats): habitat loss (85%), exotic species (50%), pollution (24%), overexploitation (17%), and disease (3%). Habitat loss is the single largest driver of extinction, affecting all ecosystems. Conservation concerns focus heavily on tropical rainforests and coral reefs due to their exceptionally high species richness. Habitat destruction negatively impacts terrestrial, freshwater, and marine biodiversity.

questions.q: What is the single greatest cause of species extinction according to the percentages provided?
questions.exp: The notes list 'Habitat loss (85%)' as the threat affecting the largest percentage of species, followed by exotic species (50%), pollution (24%), overexploitation (17%), and disease (3%).

questions.q: Which two biomes are of recent intense concern regarding habitat loss, and why?
opts: Tundra and desert; because they contain permafrost
Tropical rain forests and coral reefs; because they are highly species-rich
Chaparral and temperate deciduous forest; because they are highly flammable
Marshes and swamps; because they lack any producers
questions.exp: The notes state: 'Recent concern focuses on tropical rain forests and coral reefs because they are rich in species.'
